question_text: A television was purchased for £2000, and depreciates at $30\%$ p.a. for 3 years.

subparts.stem: Find the value of the television at the end of this period.
subparts.solution: $u_3 = u_0 \times (1 - d)^3 = 2000 \times (0.7)^3 \{30\% = 0.3\} = 686$. So, after 3 years the value of the television is £686.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Depreciation formula: $V = V_0(1-d)^n$, where $d$ is annual rate of depreciation.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using linear depreciation ($2000 - 3 \times 600$) instead of compounding.

subparts.stem: By how much has the television depreciated?

mark_breakdown.desc: Subtract depreciated value from original value

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Total depreciation is the difference between initial cost and final value.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Giving the final remaining value instead of the lost value.
